question: For Nintendo's first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (April 1 - June 30, 2026), what were net sales and operating profit in yen, how much did Nintendo say it recorded as a reduction of cost of sales from refunds of U.S. IEEPA tariffs, and - converting that refund at the quarter's average rate of JPY 159.38 per US dollar - what was operating profit excluding the refund and how did it compare with the prior-year quarter's JPY 56.9 billion?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) net sales JPY 517.8 billion (-9.5% y/y); (2) operating profit JPY 142.5 billion (+150.5%; prior-year JPY 56.9 billion); (3) tariff refund approximately US$300 million recorded as a reduction of cost of sales; (4) at JPY 159.38/USD the refund is about JPY 47.8 billion, so operating profit excluding it is about JPY 94.7 billion (accept JPY 92-97 billion), roughly +66% versus JPY 56.9 billion (accept +62% to +70%). The answer must flag the conversion as an approximation. Fail if the quarter is mislabelled (e.g., Jan-Mar 2027), if the refund is treated as a yen figure disclosed by Nintendo, or if operating profit ex-refund is not computed.
answer: Q1 FY3/2027 (April 1-June 30, 2026): net sales JPY 517.8 billion (-9.5%) and operating profit JPY 142.5 billion (+150.5% from JPY 56.9 billion). Nintendo said it recorded approximately US$300 million as a reduction of cost of sales for refunds of IEEPA tariffs [W11-E1]. At the average rate of JPY 159.38/USD that is about JPY 47.8 billion, so operating profit excluding the refund is about JPY 94.7 billion, still about +66% y/y. The full-year forecast (operating profit JPY 370.0 billion) was unchanged from May [W11-E1]. Switch 2 hardware sold 3.82 million units in the quarter [W11-E1].

**Question:** For Nintendo's first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (April 1 - June 30, 2026), what were net sales and operating profit in yen, how much did Nintendo say it recorded as a reduction of cost of sales from refunds of U.S. IEEPA tariffs, and - converting that refund at the quarter's average rate of JPY 159.38 per US dollar - what was operating profit excluding the refund and how did it compare with the prior-year quarter's JPY 56.9 billion?
*As of 2026-10-03*

**Interpreted as:** 'Nintendo' is read as Nintendo Co., Ltd. (Tokyo: 7974; ADR NTDOY), which reports under its own IR calendar and does not file with the SEC. Q1 FY2027 = the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (April 1 - June 30, 2026), Nintendo's fiscal year ending March 2027. 'Net sales' and 'operating profit' are Nintendo's reported (GAAP/IFRS as reported) figures in yen. 'Reduction of cost of sales from refunds of U.S. IEEPA tariffs' is the one-time benefit Nintendo disclosed for the quarter; the refund is converted to yen at the stated average rate of JPY 159.38/USD. 'Operating profit excluding the refund' = reported operating profit minus the yen-converted refund. The prior-year comparison is Q1 FY2026 (April 1 - June 30, 2025) operating profit of JPY 56.9 billion, as given in the question.

| | Net sales (JPY) | Operating profit (JPY) | IEEPA tariff refund recorded as reduction of cost of sales (USD) | IEEPA tariff refund converted at JPY 159.38/USD (JPY millions) | Operating profit excluding IEEPA tariff refund (JPY billions) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) | 517.8 billion yen [1] | 142.5 billion yen [1] | approximately 300 million U.S. dollars [1] | 47,814 [1] | 94.686 [1] |
| Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2025) | — | 56.9 billion yen [1] | — | — | — |

- Nintendo's Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) net sales were 517.8 billion yen, down 9.5% year-on-year from 572.3 billion yen in Q1 FY2026. [1]
- Nintendo's Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) operating profit was 142.5 billion yen, up 150.5% year-on-year from 56.9 billion yen in Q1 FY2026. [1]
- Nintendo disclosed that in Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) it recorded approximately 300 million U.S. dollars as a reduction of cost of sales in connection with refunds of IEEPA tariffs, and said the tariffs related to the refunds were primarily borne by the company rather than passed on to consumers through product prices. [1]
- Nintendo's Q1 FY2027 average exchange rate was JPY 159.38 per US dollar (and JPY 185.27 per euro). [1]
- Converting the approximately 300 million U.S. dollar IEEPA tariff refund at the Q1 FY2027 average rate of JPY 159.38 per US dollar gives a refund of 47,814 million yen (about 47.8 billion yen). [1]
- Subtracting the yen-converted refund from reported operating profit, Nintendo's Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) operating profit excluding the IEEPA tariff refund was 94.686 billion yen. [1]
- On that basis, Q1 FY2027 operating profit excluding the tariff refund was 66.4% higher than the prior-year Q1 FY2026 operating profit of 56.9 billion yen. [1]
- Nintendo's Q1 FY2027 gross profit margin rose 22.0 points to 54.3%, which the company attributed in part to refunds of U.S. tariffs imposed under IEEPA that had previously been recorded as cost of sales. [1]
- The Verge reported on August 6, 2026 that Nintendo's operating profit rose to 142.5 billion yen (about $902 million) between April 1 and June 30, compared with 56.9 billion yen (about $360 million) a year earlier, an increase of 150.5 percent, partly due to the $300 million tariff refund. [2]

- SEC-filed Q1 FY2027 financial statements (10-Q or equivalent) for Nintendo Co., Ltd.: Nintendo Co., Ltd. reports under its own IR calendar and does not file with the SEC, so no 10-Q/10-K exists; all figures come from Nintendo's own IR disclosures and press coverage.
